authority.scope: GTK2 scrollbar down-stepper preview capture in normal, pressed, and released states

implementation.change: For GTK2 scrollbar paint samples, dispatch the native GDK button press/release to the actual stepper. A GtkRange ACTIVE state alone did not paint the pressed bevel. Release is performed in cleanup and the full preview surface is checked against its pre-press pixels.

visible: Theme Lab with GTK2 attached canvas
native GTK3 and GTK4 gallery windows
session_capture.scope: Read-only screenshot of the existing private Xephyr desktop; no second session opened.

live_vm_snapshot.visible_content: File Manager and Terminal; Trash Can is not open

validation.pixel_method: Exact RGB comparison at 1:1, with no resizing, interpolation, or color normalization.
validation.result: The current Theme Lab GTK2 capture path now represents the native held stepper state and releases it safely. The native GTK2 normal and pressed cells match the retained SR10.4 normal/held pixels for this down arrow.

limits: This verifies only the GTK2 vertical down stepper capture path; other GTK2 controls remain in the active I167 review.
The current live VUE screen does not show Trash Can. Historical state comparison uses the retained native capture/state record from the same approved SR10.4 reference.
This is technical pixel evidence, not user visual approval or completion of I167/T04.
The adjustment uses GTK2 native events and existing KDE role-derived colors; no static final color was added.

technical_coverage_estimate.basis: Retained R233/R234 coverage remains the baseline; this closes a capture-path defect for an already measured GTK2 arrow state and does not complete another control family.

next: Continue only the authorized GTK2/I167 work after the user inspects the already-open private preview; leave other toolkit families untouched.
